cards.text: Grab your apron, friend! Today we're baking through Proverbs, short sayings from Solomon, king of Israel (Proverbs 10:1), and every line is its own little bite. First up, Solomon says, “Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler,” and friend, neither one of those is a compliment.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says whoever is led astray by wine and strong drink is wise.

cards.text: Next, the king. Solomon says the terror of a king is like the roar of a lion, and friend, if a lion roared in MY bakery, I'd be behind the oven so fast my gold base would leave skid marks.

cards.question: The terror of a king is like a lion's roar. What does Solomon say happens to whoever provokes him?

answers.text: He gets a seat at court

cards.question: Solomon says it is ___ for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.

cards.text: Then there's the slacker: planting season comes, and he does not plow. Friend, I've been saying I'll clean behind my oven for a LONG time now, so I know this guy.

cards.question: The slacker didn't plow in season. At harvest time he looks, but ___ is there.

cards.text: Now a deep one: Solomon says the intentions of a man's heart are deep waters. You can't just glance in and see the bottom.

cards.question: The intentions of a man's heart are deep waters. Who does Solomon say draws them out?

cards.text: Then Solomon says many a man proclaims his loving devotion, and everybody's ride or die. Then you ask for help moving a couch, and the group chat goes QUIET.

cards.question: With so many men proclaiming their loving devotion, what does Solomon ask who can find?
True or false: Solomon says the righteous man walks with integrity, and his children after him are blessed.

cards.text: Back to the throne: Solomon says a king who sits on a throne to judge sifts out all evil with his eyes. Like flour through a sifter, friend, except the lumps are evil.

cards.question: Then Solomon asks: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”? What answer is his question pointing to?

answers.text: No one can truly say it
Any wise man can say it

cards.text: Next, Solomon brings up differing weights and unequal measures in the marketplace. Picture a guy whose scale says your cookie box weighs LESS when he buys it from you, and MORE when he sells it to you.

cards.question: Differing weights and unequal measures are both ___ to the LORD.
Solomon says even a young man is known by his ___, whether his conduct is pure and upright.

cards.text: Back to it, friend! Solomon says ears that hear and eyes that see, the LORD has made them both.

cards.question: Solomon says do not love ___, or you will grow poor.

cards.text: Open your eyes, Solomon says, and you will have plenty of food. Friend, me and the snooze button go WAY back, and that button has never once filled a cookie box.
Now the marketplace again. A buyer looks over the goods and says, “Worthless, worthless!”

cards.question: The buyer just called the goods worthless. What does he do on the way out?
True or false: Solomon says gold and rubies are the rare treasure, and lips of knowledge are everywhere.

cards.text: Then a word about lending: if a man posts security for a stranger, take his garment, and get collateral if it's for a foreigner. Co-sign for a stranger, friend, and you might walk home without your coat.
Next up, food gained by fraud. Solomon says it's sweet to a man, at first.

cards.question: Food gained by fraud is sweet at first, but later his mouth is full of ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon talks about making plans, even plans for war.

cards.question: How does Solomon say to set plans?

cards.text: Then there's the gossip: Solomon says he who reveals secrets is a constant gossip. Tell that guy something Monday morning, and the whole block knows by lunch.

cards.question: Solomon says to ___ the one who babbles with his lips.

cards.text: Then a serious one. Solomon talks about whoever curses his father or mother.

cards.question: What does Solomon say happens to the lamp of whoever curses his father or mother?

answers.text: It goes out in deepest darkness
It passes on to his children

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says an inheritance gained quickly will be blessed in the end.

cards.text: Now a big one, friend: someone does you wrong, and Solomon says not to say, “I will avenge this evil!”

cards.question: Instead of getting revenge, what does Solomon tell you to do?

cards.text: Wait on the LORD, and He will save you. Friend, I sat in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS with nothing to do but count the dust, and the Most High still sent an angel to come get me.

cards.question: Unequal weights come up again. True or false: Solomon says dishonest scales are no good.

cards.text: Then Solomon says a man's steps are from the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: Because a man's steps are from the LORD, Solomon asks how anyone can understand his own way.

cards.text: Next, a warning about vows: you know the guy who says YES at midnight to helping you move at 6 AM, then takes it back by sunrise? Solomon has a word for that kind of thing.

cards.question: What does Solomon call a trap for a man?

answers.text: Seeking counsel before making a vow
Keeping a vow longer than needed

cards.text: Back to the king: Solomon says a wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them. That king does NOT let things slide.
Then Solomon says the spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD.

cards.question: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD. What does Solomon say that lamp does?

answers.text: It searches out his inmost being
It lights the path of the king
It guards his house at night

cards.question: Solomon comes back to the king one more time. What does he say preserves a king and maintains his throne?
Solomon says the glory of young men is their ___, and ___ hair is the splendor of the old.

cards.text: And Solomon ends the chapter with a tough one about lashes and wounds.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says lashes and wounds scour evil.

findings.problem: The card introduces Solomon as 'king of Israel' and cites Proverbs 10:1. That verse says only 'The proverbs of Solomon.' The title 'king of Israel' comes from Proverbs 1:1, so the reference doesn't support the fact it's attached to.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'Solomon says many a man proclaims his loving devotion, and everybody's ride or die' joins the joke to the Bible line in one sentence, so it reads as if Solomon said 'everybody's ride or die.' It also stretches 'Many a man' into 'everybody.' The verse should be told on its own, with the group-chat comparison kept separate.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The drawer comparison doesn't match the core action of 20:22, which is choosing not to take revenge and waiting on the LORD. In the backstory, Dorin didn't know the LORD and had given up while he was in the drawer. Presenting his drawer years as an example of waiting on the LORD adds something new to his story, and the comparison doesn't line up with what the verse says.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Stop 3 has almost no laugh-out-loud moments. Only card 7 has a real joke. Cards 5, 10 and 14 are flat one-line setups, and card 9's 'does NOT let things slide' is mild. Several stop 2 cards (1, 8, 10, 14) have the same problem. These lines read like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question 'What does Solomon call a trap for a man?' never says it's about vows or dedicating something. The context is only on the story card before it, which the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Seeking counsel before making a vow' isn't believable as a trap. The baker was just taught in 20:18 (stop 2, card 11) to set plans by consultation. The other wrong answer, 'Keeping a vow longer than needed', is also weak. Both wrong answers stand out next to the right one, which repeats the story card's setup.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The joke uses the same 'helping you move' premise as stop 1, card 10 (the couch and the group chat). Using the same everyday scenario twice in one walkthrough weakens the second joke.
findings.question: Should a walkthrough avoid reusing the same everyday joke premise (like asking a friend to help you move) on more than one card, unless it's an intentional callback?
